30	
31	## Checks
32	
33	Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
34	converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
35	not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.
36	
37	| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| `core-declared` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
40	| `rules-index-current` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
41	| `claudinite-isolation` | high | complexity | check: blocking |
42	| `conformance-workflow` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
43	| `conformance-work-scope` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
44	| `scheduler-workflow-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
45	| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
46	| `task-declaration-matches-folder` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
47	| `task-code-work-env` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
48	| `task-phase-discipline` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |
49	
50	What goes wrong when one fires:
51	
52	- `core-declared` — this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-checks.json`, so none of the rules above run and the session cannot tell.
53	- `rules-index-current` — the generated index is missing, stale or unimported: the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session.
54	- `claudinite-isolation` — the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` [barrier](../barriers/README.md) edge).
55	- `conformance-workflow` — nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands.
56	- `conformance-work-scope` — CI gates the tree but not the change, so every commit-scoped rule is enforced only where a session's Stop hook happens to run.
57	- `scheduler-workflow-shape` — the vendored scheduler's cron, concurrency or dispatch guard has drifted: staggering, double-run safety or manual runs break.
58	- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal, so the task never fires or fires wrong.
59	- `task-declaration-matches-folder` — a declaration disagrees with its folder: discovery drops it into `errors` and every run keeps reporting healthy without it.
60	- `task-code-work-env` — a task reads a `CLAUDINITE_*` variable code-work never sets, so a parameter (a scope filter, a dry-run switch) silently never arrives and the run goes green in its most dangerous mode.
61	- `task-phase-discipline` — a task decides not to run after its precondition already said run, hiding the decision from the run records.
62	
63	The scope cuts the other way too: a rule about how the **canon's own** content is maintained is not
64	this pack's, however much it looks like one. `catalog-completeness` — `packs/README.md` lists every
65	`packs/<name>/` — reads as Claudinite machinery and is not: it can only fire in the corpus repo, and
66	what it guards is a hand-maintained index, not a member's status. It stays in
67	[basics](../basics/README.md) with the other doc-integrity rules.
68	
69	## Skills
70	
71	| Skill | For |
72	|---|---|
73	| [`adopt-claudinite`](skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md) | setting a project up on Claudinite for the first time — mount, hooks, checks, skills — and re-baselining one to pick up updates |
74	| [`adopt-pack`](skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) | adding a pack to a repo that already runs Claudinite: declare, interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land |
75	
76	The adoption skills bundle two more checks of the same kind, over the answers a member stores
77	against each declared pack's questions:
78	
79	| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `adoption-answers-pending` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
82	| `interview-answer-stale` | low | complexity | check: advisory |
83	
84	## Tasks
85	
86	| Task | frequency | Runs when |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| `update` | daily (02:00 anchor) | the mount is behind the canon, or a declared pack moved |
89	| `adopt-requested-packs` | daily | the repo carries an open pack-adoption request |
90	
91	`update` is the per-repo self-refresh — the task that converges a member's mount and stamps it. It
92	is why `core-declared` is blocking: a member runs `update` from its **vendored** copy, and
93	`discoverTasks` finds only a literally-declared pack's tasks, so a repo that loses this pack's entry
94	loses its self-refresh, and nothing is left that could deliver it one. That is also why the task
95	arrived here a change later than the rest of the pack — it moved only once every non-dormant member's
96	declaration had been read back and confirmed to carry `core`.

One directory per task — `<pack>/tasks/<name>/` — holding **`task.mjs`** (the

scheduled-task shape of the unattended-agents routine-folder convention; the
issue-driven-dispatch security rule (the issue is data, the task path is
code-validated, agent_model/expected_outcome come from the repo) lives with that
skill's agent practices.

Refs #972. **Mostly superseded by [#1013](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1013)** — this PR is now the small residue it left behind, rebuilt on current `main` (past the [#1029](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1029) pack rename). Down from 24 files to 4.

#1013 did the substance and did it better than my draft: the explicit "a cadence is one way an occurrence is created, not what a task is" paragraph, `manual` as a first-class value, the event-driven-work-is-a-task route in the cron rule, and an exception clause that names the OIDC case directly. Everything I had written for the doc body is dropped in favour of it.

Two carriers of the old framing sit outside the passages it rewrote.

## 1. The rule that routes readers to the contract

`claudinite-growth/RULES.md` still opened **"Writing or changing a scheduled task"**. That line is loaded in every session in every declaring repo — it is the most-read sentence on the subject, and it still carried the assumption the contract itself has stopped making. It now says *task*, states the code-work default, and gains a second rule for the reader who wants a job to run in Actions and would otherwise reach for a workflow. Its trigger is phrased as the act they're performing, so it fires before the workflow gets authored rather than after.

## 2. "The task folder"

Still made `task.md` *the* worker ("the worker spec the executing agent follows") and `agent_model: none` a substitution away from it. Flipped to lead with the worker being code — a sibling `.mjs` the executor runs as code-work, the item closing on that subprocess's outcome, no session started — with the agent as the escalation. The leftover "This is the **scheduled-task** shape of the unattended-agents routine-folder convention" goes with it.

## Folders touched

- **`packs/claudinite-growth/`** — the two prose fixes above, in `RULES.md` and `scheduled-tasks.md`, plus the pack version bump.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2143 pass, 0 fail.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs --changed --base origin/main` — exit 0.

## Deliberately not included

**The filename.** The doc is titled "Tasks — the per-project work mechanism" and lives at `scheduled-tasks.md`. Renaming completes #1013's stated goal but is a ~20-file sweep touching five checks' `doc:` fields, and #1013 chose not to — so it is a separate call, not something to slip in here.

**The one-cron invariant**, unchanged as before: I read your "annoying" as the framing, which #1013 has now fixed in the doc body.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Text & file manipulation

Portable practices for searching, extracting, and rewriting text across a repository's files — grep/sed sweeps, renames and relocations, and the silent reference-breakage they leave behind. These are project-agnostic; they're the mechanics half of editing a codebase as text. (General software-engineering practices live in [the basics pack's RULES.md](../../RULES.md); the merge-time relocation traps — git's rename detection, references that break with no conflict across a merge — live in [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md), "Merging across a file relocation".)

- When you relocate a file's *content or responsibility* into a new home — folding a doc into a pack, moving a function to another module, absorbing a routine into a skill — the original is now **redundant surface**, and reducing it to a tombstone stub (`# retired — see X`) is not finishing the job: the stub still costs a read, drifts from its replacement, and misleads anyone who lands on it. Delete the emptied original in the *same* change, and treat "did this move make anything else dead?" as a standing question after every restructure — the source you copied *from* is the first suspect. Don't wait to be told a leftover is redundant; a relocation that leaves two homes for one thing isn't done.
- When renaming `foo/` → `bar/foo/`, a naive repo-wide string-replace of `foo/` → `bar/foo/` causes two silent corruptions: files already under the target namespace double-prefix (`bar/foo/file` → `bar/bar/foo/file`), and external URLs containing the string `foo/` get rewritten. Scope the replace to only internal path strings that need it, or do the replace then make a targeted post-pass reverting matches inside URLs and already-correct paths.
- A grep/sed rename pass over a path (`foo/bar/baz.js`) won't match it when built from `path.join` segments (`path.join(__dirname, "foo", "bar", "baz.js")`) or wrapped across a line in a comment — those references survive the rewrite and break only at run time. After a mechanical path-rename pass, also search for the path's individual segment tokens and run the test suite; the test suite, not the grep, surfaces a missed reference.
- An ordered specific→catch-all path rewrite can half-convert a reference the specific rule's trailing slash missed. Renaming `old/sub/` → `new/leaf/` with a slash-anchored rule (`s#old/sub/#new/leaf/#`) plus a catch-all for the parent (`s#old/#new/#`), a reference *without* the trailing slash (`path.join(root, "old/sub")`, a bare `git add old/sub`, a prose mention) escapes the specific rule, and the catch-all then rewrites only its **parent** — `old/sub` → `new/sub`, not `new/leaf` — a half-converted path that breaks at run time, not at the rewrite. Match both the slashed and bare forms, then grep the bare-dir form (at a quote / paren / line-end) and run the tests.
- After `git mv`, re-read the file at its **new** path before rewriting it — an editing tool that tracks reads by path treats the moved path as never-seen and silently refuses the write, leaving the file stale (a failure that surfaces much later, far from its cause). When the move and the rewrite share a batch of tool calls, check each result individually; a single refused write is easy to miss in a batch.
- To exclude a directory's own files from a reference search, filter by file **path**, not `grep -v` on line content: `grep -rn foo/bar | grep -v foo/bar/` (meant to drop the directory's own files) *also* drops every legitimate full-path reference elsewhere, silently undercounting. Exclude by pathspec instead — `git grep -n foo/bar -- . ':(exclude)foo/bar'` — which filters on which file is searched, not on what each matching line happens to contain.
- To exclude vendored, synced, or generated files from a **structural** check that walks a tree (an orphan/reachability scan, a doc audit, a lint), derive the file set from git's tracked list (e.g. `git ls-files`) rather than a filesystem walk with a hardcoded path to skip — it can't desync when the artifact moves, and it stays correct when a new ignored directory appears. (Sibling of the pathspec-exclude rule above: that one separates a directory from its own files within a search; this one separates owned content from vendored/generated content.)
- A zero-hit grep proves absence only at the case you searched. Code normalizes tokens away from prose case — an uppercase data table (`'KNEW'`), a SCREAMING_SNAKE constant, a lowercased slug — so a case-sensitive `grep knew` finds nothing and reads as "not in the codebase" while the entry sits right there, and a conclusion built on that phantom absence compounds. Before concluding a token is absent, re-run with `-i`; when history should have touched it, `git log -S<token>` is the cross-check that catches the miss.
- When writing file content captured from a script or command output, use the `Write` tool directly — never `cp` from an internal Claude Code path (`/root/.claude/projects/...`). The tool-results paths are harness-internal and inaccessible to shell commands; referencing them via Bash triggers a permission prompt. Capture the output in context and pass it to `Write`.

input.title: A check's `doc:` field can dangle silently — nothing resolves it against the tree
input.body:
## The finding

`task-declaration-shape`'s `doc:` pointed at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/scheduled-tasks.md`. No file has been at that path since #1029 moved the packs — the doc has lived in `packs/claudinite-growth/` throughout. The finding rendered a path to nothing, and nothing noticed.

Found incidentally while renaming that doc in #975 (fixed there). The other four `doc:` fields happened to be right.

## Why it is silent

`doc:` is display-only — it is rendered into a finding's `More:` line, never opened. So a wrong value costs nothing at author time, nothing in CI, and nothing at runtime; it only misleads the session that follows the pointer, which is exactly the session already dealing with a failing check.

## Why it will recur

Both ways it breaks are routine here:

- **A pack move.** #1029 renamed `core` → `claudinite-lifecycle` and `grow_with_claudinite` → `claudinite-growth` and relocated the contract between them. That is what created this one.
- **A doc rename.** #975 renames `scheduled-tasks.md` → `tasks.md`; a `doc:` missed by the sweep would dangle the same way.

That is twice in two changes, which is the bar for a guard rather than a fix.

## Shape

A check over `packs/**/declared-checks.json` and the `doc:` field of each `*.mjs` check definition, asserting the referenced path exists in `git ls-files`. Deterministic, no judgment, and it fails loudly on exactly the two moves above.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the same guard should cover `More:`-style pointers in `fix` strings and the relative links in pack `README.md`/`RULES.md` — the doc-rename sweep in #975 had to hand-verify all of those too, and a link into another pack's directory is the shape most likely to rot after a pack move.

input.title: Rename the task doc to match its title, and carry the split into the rule
input.body:
Refs #972. Mostly superseded by [#1013](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1013), which did the substance and did it better; this is the residue it left, rebuilt on current `main` (past [#1029](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1029)'s pack rename). Three carriers of the old framing sat outside the passages #1013 rewrote.

## 1. The filename

The doc is titled *"Tasks — the per-project work mechanism"* and lived at `scheduled-tasks.md`, so the mount listing still announced the assumption the doc had stopped making. Renamed to `tasks.md`, 23 path references swept.

Per the `repo-text-sweeps` rules I checked for the failure modes a mechanical rename leaves: no `path.join`-built or line-wrapped references (none exist), then re-resolved **every** `tasks.md` reference in the tree against the filesystem rather than trusting the grep.

## 2. The rule that routes readers to the contract

`claudinite-growth/RULES.md` still opened **"Writing or changing a scheduled task"** — the most-read sentence on the subject, loaded in every session in every declaring repo. It now says *task*, states the code-work default, and gains a second rule for the reader who wants a job to run in Actions and would otherwise reach for a workflow, keyed to the act they are performing so it fires before the workflow gets authored.

## 3. "The task folder"

Still made `task.md` *the* worker ("the worker spec the executing agent follows") and `agent_model: none` a substitution away from it. Flipped to lead with the worker being code, with the agent as escalation; the leftover "the **scheduled-task** shape of the unattended-agents convention" goes with it.

## A dangling reference the sweep surfaced

`task-declaration-shape`'s `doc:` has pointed at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/scheduled-tasks.md` since #1029 moved the packs — **no file has been at that path since**, and nothing caught it, because `doc:` is rendered into a finding's `More:` line and never opened. Repointed here, and every other `doc:` field verified against the tree.

Filed as #1043: it will recur on the next pack move or doc rename, and a check that resolves `doc:` against `git ls-files` is deterministic. Not built here — that guard belongs in its own change.

## Folders touched

- **`packs/claudinite-growth/`** — the doc renamed `scheduled-tasks.md` → `tasks.md` and its "task folder" section flipped to code-first; the two prose rules in `RULES.md`; the corrected `doc:` in `task-declaration-shape.mjs`.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`, `packs/github-actions/`, `packs/product-wiki/`, `packs/sheepdog/`** — path references to the renamed doc, plus the `scheduled-task contract` → `task contract` wording where it named the doc.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Writing Claudinite skills

A corpus skill is a harness-matched trigger (frontmatter `name` + a tight `description`) plus the body the agent needs at usage time — well under 500 lines, and nothing a deterministic mechanism could carry instead (the promotion ladder in [engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md) decides). A skill may own the rules that validate its action — `checks.mjs` beside the SKILL.md, one module per rule, fixture tests beside them; shape and the relevance-first gate in [engine/checks/README.md](../../../../../../engine/checks/README.md#adding-a-rule). Ownership is placement: the skill lives in exactly one owning pack's `skills/` (#385) — there is no skill catalog; the pack's own README names what it bundles. Instruction-writing *quality* — how agents actually follow docs — is [authoring-agent-docs](../../../../../../packs/basics/skills/authoring-agent-docs/SKILL.md)' turf; this skill is the corpus mechanics.

1	# claudinite-growth
2	
3	Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
4	lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
5	Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
6	existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.
7	
8	This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
9	lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
10	**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
11	that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.
12	
13	Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
14	scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:
15	
16	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
19	| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | weekly, when the canon or the project's local packs moved in the week | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
20	| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
21	| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | weekly (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |
22	| `rule-revalidation` ([tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md](tasks/rule-revalidation/task.md)) | weekly | a reviewed PR correcting rules whose environment claim no longer probes true |
23	
24	(Plus two agentless daily tasks over the conversation-logs branch: [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md),
25	described below, and `logs-prune` — retention, [tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs](tasks/logs-prune/worker.mjs).)
26	
27	## Extraction is one task over two sources
28	
29	`growth-extract` is the whole capture stage, and it runs **three skills** in order:
30	
31	1. [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) over the window's commits, merged
32	   PRs and issue discussion;
33	2. [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) over the logs captured
34	   from working sessions;
35	3. [prose-to-checks](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) over the prose **that run just wrote**, to see
36	   whether any of it upgrades to a check before the PR opens.
37	
38	Everything lands in **one** PR, delivered to land where the repo's delivery settings allow
39	(`engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`). The two extraction halves used to be two tasks firing in
40	the same nightly anchor against the same local packs; they share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder
41	and the dedup surface ([extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)), so the split bought nothing
42	and cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was
43	concurrently writing.
44	
45	The third step is why the standing `prose-to-checks-sweep` is **weekly**: fresh prose is already
46	offered a conversion the night it is written, so what the sweep sees is a backlog that moves on a
47	weekly clock.
48	
49	A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
50	promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "claudinite-growth", "config": { "promote": false } }`
51	— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).
52	
53	## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in the daily task, retention
54	
55	The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions**, replacing the old in-session post-merge
56	lessons pass. Capture and extraction split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session
57	transcript, so it runs in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only
58	reads the already-pushed logs, so it is the conversation half of the ordinary `growth-extract`
59	scheduled task — the logs branch is *in the repo*, so reading it, committing lessons to local packs,
60	and pruning are plain local git on the working tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the
61	GitHub MCP tools.
62	
63	1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
64	   Right after a merge lands:
65	   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
66	   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
67	   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
68	   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
69	   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
70	   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
71	   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
72	   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
73	   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
74	   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
75	   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
76	   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
77	   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
78	   on, so `pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
79	   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
80	   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
81	1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
82	   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
83	   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
84	   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
85	   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
86	   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
87	   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that

90	   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for the extract to post its exchange
91	   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
92	   **Unattended sessions capture through the same step, deliberately not through the hook.** A
93	   scheduled task's executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is exactly
94	   the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so the executor runs the engine's runner itself as its
95	   last step and names its work item in `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`, which this step uses in
96	   place of `0`. Those logs therefore file under the task that ran (the item's title
97	   names `pack/task`), and the work no human watched becomes as countable as the work one did.
98	2. **The pass — the conversation half of [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)**
99	   (precondition: a substantive merge; local git on the repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It
100	   applies the [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) skill (the

input.title: Make the task contract a skill, and fix the framing it still carried
input.body:
Refs #972. Rebuilt on current `main` (past #1051).

## The move

`packs/claudinite-growth/scheduled-tasks.md` is *how to write a task* — the declaration's fields, the two phases, the precondition rule, ordering between tasks, how a work item converges. That is a procedure wanted at authoring time, not prose every session should carry, and today it is reached only by following a link out of `RULES.md` or a check's `More:` line.

It is now **[`skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/github-pages-deploy-action-8l1dtr/packs/claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md)** — invocable by description rather than found by link. Moved whole (293 lines, well inside the skill budget), frontmatter added, wired into the pack's `skills` list and named in its README beside the three task checks that judge against it. No tombstone at the old path: two homes for one thing is what the move exists to remove.

Verified it actually mounts — the skill was offered in the session's own skill list on the next start, with the trigger description firing on "writing or changing a `task.mjs`".

## Framing fixes riding along

#1013 stopped the doc calling tasks scheduled-only, but three carriers sat outside the passages it rewrote:

- **`RULES.md`** — prose every session in every declaring repo loads — still opened *"Writing or changing a **scheduled** task"*. It now says task, states the code-work default, and gains a second rule for the reader who wants a job to run in Actions and would otherwise author a workflow, keyed to the act they're performing so it fires before the workflow exists.
- **"The task folder"** still made `task.md` *the* worker and `agent_model: none` a substitution away from it. Flipped: the worker is code by default, the agent is the escalation.
- **The title**, now "Writing a task".

## A dangling reference the sweep surfaced

`task-declaration-shape`'s `doc:` has pointed at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/scheduled-tasks.md` since #1029 moved the packs — **no file has been there since**, and nothing caught it, because `doc:` is rendered into a finding's `More:` line and never opened. Repointed, and every other `doc:` field verified against the tree. Filed separately as #1043; the guard is its own change.

## Folders touched

- **`packs/claudinite-growth/`** — the doc becomes the `writing-tasks` skill (frontmatter, retitle, code-first "task folder", relocated outbound link); the two prose rules in `RULES.md`; the skill wired into `pack.mjs`; the corrected `doc:` in `task-declaration-shape.mjs` and the reference in `task-declaration-matches-folder.mjs`.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`** — the `doc:` in `conformance-workflow.mjs`, and the cross-pack pointer that named the contract by filename.
- **`packs/github-actions/`, `packs/product-wiki/`, `packs/sheepdog/`** — references repointed at the skill, and `scheduled-task contract` → `task contract` where the phrase named the doc.
- Versions bumped on all five packs.

`docs/per-project-scheduling/` is a historical record — link targets only, content untouched.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2169 pass, 0 fail.
- `check_the_work --changed --base origin/main` — exit 0.
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking (62 advisory, all pre-existing).
- Every `writing-tasks` link and every check `doc:` field re-resolved against the tree, and the skill confirmed mounted.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `claudinite-growth` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
